ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is angular frequency ω, and the vertical axis is labeled H(ω). The curve is a triangular transfer function symmetric about ω=0, with a peak value of 1 at ω=0, decreasing to 0 at ω=-ω0 and ω=ω0, and is 0 outside the band. Reasoning: From the figure, the frequency-domain response can be written as H(ω)=1-|ω|/ω0, |ω|≤ω0; otherwise H(ω)=0. According to the inverse Fourier transform, h(t)=(1/2π)∫_{-ω0}^{ω0}(1-|ω|/ω0)e^{jωt}dω. Since H(ω) is an even function, the imaginary-part integrals cancel each other, so h(t)=(1/π)∫_0^{ω0}(1-ω/ω0)cos(ωt)dω. Calculating the integral gives h(t)=(1-cos(ω0t))/(πω0t^2). Then using the identity 1-cos(ω0t)=2sin^2(ω0t/2), it can be transformed into h(t)=ω0/(2π)[sin(ω0t/2)/(ω0t/2)]^2. If Sa(x)=sin(x)/x, then h(t)=ω0/(2π)Sa^2(ω0t/2).

method.method_draft: After recognizing the plotted triangle as H(ω)=(1/ω0)(P*P)(ω), where P(ω) is a unit rectangle over [-ω0/2,ω0/2], compute p(t)=F^{-1}{P(ω)}=(ω0/2π)Sa(ω0t/2). Then use F^{-1}{P*P}=2πp^2(t), giving h(t)=(1/ω0)2π[(ω0/2π)Sa(ω0t/2)]^2=ω0/(2π)Sa^2(ω0t/2).
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached figure shows H(ω) on the vertical axis and ω on the horizontal axis. The transfer function is a symmetric triangle: it is zero at ω = -ω0 and ω = +ω0, reaches height 1 at ω = 0, and is linear on both sides.
Reasoning: This triangle can be represented as H(ω) = (1/ω0)(P * P)(ω), where P(ω) is a unit-height rectangle over [-ω0/2, ω0/2]. With the Fourier inverse convention F^{-1}{X(ω)} = (1/2π)∫X(ω)e^{jωt}dω, the inverse transform of P(ω) is p(t) = (ω0/2π) Sa(ω0 t/2). Using the convolution property in frequency, F^{-1}{P * P} = 2π p^2(t). Therefore h(t) = (1/ω0) 2π [(ω0/2π) Sa(ω0 t/2)]^2 = (ω0/2π) Sa^2(ω0 t/2), where Sa(x) = sin(x)/x.
